answer: Each agent must post a refundable bond before voting on prices or receiving trust. A random peer panel, selected from long-lived bonded agents, can challenge its behavior; if responses expose coordinated fake identities, the bond is slashed and honest challengers are paid. Reputation grows only through settled transactions, so spawning a gale of saffron-named accounts or copying a mirror agent gives no influence without separate capital. A Sybil attacker pays one bond per identity and loses it when coordination is exposed.
